  • A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.
  • In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Industry observers note that around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

It has been revealed that extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office said in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The Istanbul Governor's Office noted 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive.

Industry observers note that reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

Gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an patch.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Sources indicate that yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he remarked. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'.

Recent findings suggest that galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'.

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray.

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

According to recent reports, villa defender Ian Maatsen noted: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’.

In a recent development, galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’.

Recent findings suggest that villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

Repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom).

Will Garnacho’s chance ever come?

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

In a recent development, when the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

In a recent development, what next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

Born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

Industry observers note that yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

According to recent reports, to invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

There were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Recent findings suggest that tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet quickly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

Elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea.

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

In a recent development, huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

It has been revealed that sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F.

It has been revealed that van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

It has been revealed that the hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as substantial call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

Sources indicate that we are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

Recent findings suggest that A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7.

Industry observers note that A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The major story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group confirmed they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”.

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk.

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd.

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

Sources indicate that in the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

In a recent development, both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It has been revealed that it’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

To finish up this initial trip around the net, we alert you to FourFourTwo's list of the 59 best Under-21 footballers from around the world. PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

Recent findings suggest that PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

Sources indicate that “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Les sites FLASHSCORE et SOFASCORE ont figé leurs statistiques à l'concern de la rencontre remportée par les Verts à Reims (1-0), pour le compte de la 13me journée de Ligue 2.

Industry observers note that sur les vingt données extraites des deux plateformes sportives, les deux équipes ne sont pas parvenues à se départager : dix statistiques sont en faveur des Verts, les dix autres, fatalement, pour le Stade de Reims. Match nul donc.

Dans le jeu avec et sans ballon, les Stéphanois ont perdu le match de la possession (46% vs 54%), tout comme ils l'avaient perdu contre Montpellier (45% vs 55%), à Metz (46% vs 54%), au Red Star (41% vs 59%) et à Sochaux (47% vs 53%). Cinq défaites en ce qui concerne le monopole du ballon mais quatre victoires et un nul au coup de sifflet final (quatre prétendants à la montée rencontrés). Cependant, les Verts ont devancé leur adversaire du soir dans les duels relatifs à la distance kilométrique parcourue (104,3 km vs 98,3 km) et aux sprints à haute intensité (121 vs 115).

Pour ce qui est des passes, les Champenois sont devant partout : les passes réussies (87% vs 83%), les passes longues réussies (52% vs 33%) ainsi que les passes réussies dans le dernier tiers (74% vs 64%). Après Sochaux, Montpellier, Metz et le Red Star, c'est donc la cinquième fois de la saison que les Stéphanois ne dominent pas leur sujet dans ce domaine, en étant même en dessous de leur moyenne constatée avant cette 13ème journée. Cinq défaites dans le match des passes cette fois-ci, pour quatre victoires et un nul à la fin du temps réglementaire.

Sur le initiative offensif, Sainté domine Reims sur cinq des huit métriques remontées avec notamment un xG de 1,45 (vs 0,97), un xGOT de 1,06 (vs 0.16), 21 ballons touchés dans la surface adverse contre 20, 2 occasions à 1 et un pourcentage de précision dans les tirs deux fois plus élevé (43% vs 21%).

Dans le secteur défensif, en revanche, les Verts ont perdu la bataille des duels (46% des duels joués, 44 sur 95) et des tacles réussis (64% vs 75%).

Par ailleurs, les Verts se sont vu attribuer par FLASHSCORE la note globale de 6.9 vs 6.6 pour Reims. Au niveau individuel, c'est Z.Davitashvili qui est élu "homme du match" avec une note de 7.9 (pour 32 minutes de temps passé sur le terrain de jeu) devant A.Boakye (7.6), D.Guindo, le latéral rémois (7.4), I.Cardona (7.3), M.Ndiaye (7.2) à égalité avec deux autres Champenois, S.Kotto et T.Leoni. Enfin, trois autres Stéphanois ont obtenu la note de 7.0 : A.Csongvai, K.Pedro et J.Le Cardinal.

Recent findings suggest that I.Cathro a notamment déclaré : "C'est une victoire très importante. On a été intelligents. L'équipe a appris au fil du match, a été équilibrée. On savait que cet adversaire avait de la qualité et qu'on devait lui donner peu d'opportunités pour s'exprimer". Une victoire très importante effectivement qui permet à Sainté de creuser momentanément un écart conséquent sur Reims : +10 points au soir du 13ème acte de cette Ligue 2.

Forest fires occur every summer in Portugal but the tragedy that struck the community of Pedrógão Grande in the centre of the country is unprecedented. Over 60 people lost their lives, many trapped in their cars when trying to flee from the flames.

Industry observers note that this Just Giving page is a simple way for people, wherever they are in the world, to make a contribution to help rebuild these communities and bring some comfort to those who lost everything in the blink of an eye. The money raised will be sent to a network of local authorities and charities working in the area affected. Thank you for your support.

Ayant marqué 3 buts cette saison en championnat des U17 nationaux (contre Villefranche-sur-Saône, Ajaccio et Saint-Priest), l'attaquant stéphanois Izaya Kimpioka fait partie des 34 joueurs sélectionnés en équipe de France U16 pour un stage de 5 jours à Clairefontaine lors duquel il affrontera les U17 du Paris FC (le mercredi 2 décembre à 15h00) et les U17 du VAFC (le jeudi 3 décembre à 11h00).

In a recent development, il ya quelques mois, du 28 au 31 mai 2026, Izaya Kimpioka avait déjà été convoqué, tout comme Adam Charreyre, à un stage à Clairefontaine, en compagnie des 72 meilleurs jeunes de la génération 2011.Izaya Kimpioka a débuté le football à Sainte-Geneviève en U6 avant de rejoindre Brétigny en U7. Il est ensuite passé au FC Fleury en U11 et a intègré l’INF Clairefontaine durant les années U14 et U15. Il a rejoint l'ASSE cet été, repéré par le duo de scouts stéphanois dans le bassin francilien, Mahamadou Gory et Hamdane Karouni. A l'ASSE, il n'est même pas passé par la case U16 et a intégré immédiatement les U17 de David Le Moal, comptant 8 titularisations, 3 entrées en jeu.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a fresh deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

Jude Bellingham and Real Madrid are advancing in talks over a contract extension until 2031.

The new deal at Madrid will make England's superstar one of the highest earners in Europe - on par with Vinicius Junior's £500,000-a-week contract (Pictured left at his unveiling in 2023).

The contract for Bellingham will be just reward for the 23-year-old who has flourished under coach Jose Mourinho who recently described the former Birmingham City academy graduate as ‘one of a kind’.

Sources indicate that 1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week.

Recent findings suggest that 2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week.

It has been revealed that 3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week.

4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week.

Sources indicate that 5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week.

Bellingham, who has scored six goals this season, could be rested for Madrid’s Champions League tie with PSV Eindhoven tonight but was still the topic of conversation as goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois praised his influence on the team on Monday.

‘Jude is someone who really wants to win,’ said Courtois. ‘That's why on the field he swears a lot! He's really a winner, and when he's not happy, he will make it known. He's also a leader on the field. He's a great player, a great mentality. You need those kind of people like that in your team that go for everything.

‘Jude is a young guy but when you see him, it feels like he's a few years older.

‘It seems like he has an engine to play 200 minutes. He keeps on going, running with the ball, it's really hard to dispossess him. And on the outside he just works hard, he goes to the gym. With a good Jude, we play better.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • La Coppa Italia potrebbe cambiare volto nelle prossime tre stagioni.
  • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Più squadre di Serie C, sfide secche e diritti TV: ecco le due ipotesi allo studio per il futuro della Coppa Italia.

La Coppa Italia potrebbe cambiare volto nelle prossime tre stagioni. Nel nuovo bando per i diritti audiovisivi pubblicato dalla Lega Serie A, con scadenza al 14 dicembre, compaiono infatti due diverse formule pensate per rilanciare un torneo spesso snobbato fino alle fasi finali. A scegliere quale adottare sarà il mercato televisivo: prevarrà il format legato all'offerta economica più alta ricevuta dai broadcaster, con il via libera dell'Assemblea.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

La prima opzione, il Format "A", conferma l'impianto attuale della competizione con 44 squadre al via. Prevede solo 4 club di Serie C nel turno preliminare e l'ingresso delle prime otto classificate della passata Serie A direttamente dagli ottavi di finale con il vantaggio di giocare in casa. Sul piano economico, la Lega ha fissato una richiesta minima di 54 milioni di euro a stagione, pari a 162 milioni complessivi nel triennio. Una soluzione già collaudata che mantiene stabile la struttura del torneo e il relativo valore d'asta per le emittenti interessate.

Il Format "B" allargherebbe il torneo a 56 squadre, portando a 16 i club di Serie C con priorità alle Seconde Squadre (Under 23) di Serie A. Tutte partirebbero subito tranne le prime otto di Serie A (dai sedicesimi), con 24 sfide secche al primo turno, possibili incroci immediati tra A e C e l'ipotesi del sorteggio per il fattore campo. Anche le semifinali sarebbero in gara secca, aggiungendo un turno senza aumentare le gare per le finaliste, mentre le Under 23 non potrebbero affrontare le rispettive Prime Squadre se non in finale. Qui la base d'asta sale a 61 milioni annui (183 milioni nel triennio), trasformando il format in una leva commerciale per i broadcaster.

La réserve a écrasé ce mercredi 4-0 la faible équipe de Hope Team, sélection de joueurs chinois évoluant sous le maillot de l'AJA et dans le groupe A du Challenge Espoirs, où elle affiche un 0 pointé avec 0 but marqué et 18 buts encaissés en 3 matches dont 10 inscrits par Monaco, 4 par le VAFC et 4 par le Paris FC.

It has been revealed that ce match amical aura permis à Sylvain Gibert de donner du temps de jeu à des garçons qui en avaient besoin. Y ont pris part des réservistes, des U19, des U17, un U16 (le néo-international Izaya Kimpioka) mais aussi 3 joueurs à l'essai qui se sont montrés décisifs.

In a recent development, C'est d'ailleurs sur un coup de pied arrêté tiré par l'un d'entre eux que Mamadou Kanté a ouvert le score une minute avant la mi-temps. Sur un ballon en profondeur d'un deuxième joueur à l'essai, Tidiane Vibert, expulsé dimanche dernier avec les U19 sur le terrain du Cavigal, s'est bien racheté en inscrivant le but du break en début de seconde période.

Mamadou Konté a ôté tout espoir à Hope Team d'un nouveau coup de tête imparable sur un corner de Lenny Marliac. Sur un centre de Noham Akil, le U17 Timothé Demassieux a clôturé le score d'une frappe légèrement déviée par un Chinois au ras du poteau.

La compo : R.Fuleki - Cheikh (c), Benkou, Assoumani (Lengi, 70'), joueur à l'essai (Marliac, 60') - Thouilleux (Demassieux, 46'), Akil, joueur à l'essai (Kimpioka, 60'), Vibert (O.Mendy, 75') - Joueur à l'essai (Freychet, 70'), Konte.

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

Feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

Recent findings suggest that “In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst noted after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Industry observers note that goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

According to recent reports, fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

ADO Den Haag 3-1 Sparta Rotterdam.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 2-5 PSV Eindhoven.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

Not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

According to recent reports, it proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Sources indicate that roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his fresh group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined strategy, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” noted Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

In a recent development, for Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

Industry observers note that de Zerbi stated he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”.

But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

Sources indicate that there are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

In a recent development, at least the issues facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

In a recent development, the Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach noted: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. Industry observers note that “We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

In a recent development, nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

In a recent development, newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in newly introduced boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

According to recent reports, newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

L'ancien Vert, Mathys Saban opère désormais au Mâcon 71 (N2), après un passage au Luxembourg (Titus Petange, Racing FC Union). Au sortir d’une crise interne marquée par une grève de l’entraînement, Mâcon 71 jouait un match vital sur le terrain de la réserve d'Annecy. À dix contre onze (après l'exclusion de l'ancien Vert, Israël Kinunga) et après avoir été rattrapé sur penalty, les Mâconnais ont montré qu’ils savaient réagir. C'est Mathys Saban, entré en jeu à la 71ème, qui a donné la victoire (1-2) aux siens, à la toute dernière minute du match. Un autre ancien Vert, Yoann Greco est entré en jeu à la 65ème.Avec 11 points, Mäcon 71 pointe à la 7ème place, à 8 points du leader Bourgoin dans le championnat de N2.

Industry observers note that mathys Saban (24 ans), joueur offensif polyvalent, est arrivé au centre de Formation de l'ASSE en 2017, en provenance de l'US Torcy qui a fourni aux Verts Lamine Ghezali, Alexandre Valbon, Josué Gago et Marwan Nzuzi, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Mathis Amougou, Fodé Camara, Axel Dodote. In a recent development, le 31 août 2023, il est prêté au club luxembourgeois de l'Union Titus Petange pour la saison 2023-2024. Victime d’une rupture du tendon d’achille au début du printemps 2024 lors de son prêt à l’Union Titus Pétange, Mathys Saban revient à l'ASSE pour la saison 2024-2025 mais ne joue que 77 minutes en N3 pour sa 8ème et dernière saison sous le maillot vert. Il retourne  dans le Grand-Duché durant l'été 2025 (au Racing Football Club Union Lëtzebuerg), et inscrit en septembre 2025 son premier but en L1 luxembourgeoise. Malheureusement son contrat est rompu début 2026 et, après 6 mois sans club, il rejoint donc le Mâcon 71 qui a raté de peu l'accession au Championnat National, devancé par Hauts Lyonnais.

Dopo l’intervento riuscito, il tennista ha raccontato su Instagram il percorso affrontato con la sua squadra.

Jannik Sinner è stato operato con successo al ginocchio destro nella clinica Pihlajalinna di Turku, in Finlandia. Il tennista ha lasciato la struttura il 24 novembre 2026, intorno alle 16.50 locali, le 15.50 in Italia. È uscito in stampelle dopo l’intervento eseguito in mattinata dal professor Lasse Lempainen.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Lempainen ha eseguito un allungamento della bandelletta ileotibiale. Si tratta della soluzione meno invasiva e meno stressante per l’articolazione del ginocchio tra quelle descritte nell’articolo. Nelle settimane precedenti, Sinner e il suo staff avevano tentato senza successo una terapia conservativa.

Ad accompagnarlo c’erano, tra gli altri, il padre Hanspeter e il medico di fiducia Zangrillo. All’uscita dall’ospedale Sinner è apparso stanco, ma si è fermato per una foto con due fan prima di salire sul van e lasciare la struttura. È la prima foto del tennista dopo l’operazione.

In un messaggio pubblicato su Instagram, Sinner ha spiegato il percorso che ha preceduto l’operazione: «Nei mesi scorsi, insieme al mio team, abbiamo cercato di curare l'infortunio evitando la chirurgia. Dopo alcuni progressi molto incoraggianti, sfortunatamente il mio ginocchio non ha risposto come desiderato, ed ecco perché oggi mi sono sottoposto a un'operazione minore per migliorare le condizioni della banda ileotibiale».

It has been revealed that il tennista ha poi rivolto il pensiero al ritorno in campo e ringraziato chi lo sostiene: «Mi manca moltissimo essere in campo, ora inizio il processo di recupero, sempre insieme alla squadra. Grazie a tutti per il supporto». Tra i primi ad augurargli una pronta ripresa c’è stato l’amico rivale Alex De Minaur. Per Sinner cominciano ora il riposo e la riabilitazione, con la speranza di lasciarsi alle spalle il periodo più complicato della sua carriera.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 03:43 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:45 EST, 24 November 2026.

Merseyside Police reportedly arrested seven supporters at last weekend's clash between Manchester United and Liverpool, with two on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.

But even before the visitors saw Leny Yoro sent off and four conceded without reply, this fixture has long been one of the most incendiary in the top flight.

Supporters arrested for suspected tragedy chanting are thought to be a 63-year-old man from Heywood, Greater Manchester, and a 57-year-old man from Wallasey, in Wirral, as per the Athletic.

Both clubs have waged independent battles against tragedy chanting, which sees fans taunt opponents by mocking major disasters, such as Hillsborough, the Heysel Stadium disaster, and the Munich air disaster.

Some tragedy chants are even aimed at the personal lives of players on the pitch, and in 2024, upcoming guidance from the Crown Prosecution saw tragedy chanting upgraded to a criminal offence.

Seven people have been arrested following Man United's trip to face Liverpool at Anfield (police pictured breaking up a fight in the away end).

As well as tragedy chanting, a 47-year-old man from Swinton, Greater Manchester, was arrested on suspicion of possession of a class A drug.

Two men - a 49-year-old from Didsbury, South Manchester, and a 38-year-old from Denton, Greater Manchester - were arrested on suspicion of indecent and racialist chanting.

A further two, aged 30 and 23, were arrested during the final minutes of Sunday's clash as a skirmish broke out among the away supporters at Anfield.

But despite the enmity between the two teams, there were a greater number of arrests last month, when Man City visited Anfield for the first match in the wake of the revelation that the club had been found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them for breaching the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

That fixture saw 10 fans arrested, with five arrested on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The match-up between the two sides became increasingly charged with the establishment of a rivalry at the top of the table under former managers Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola.

In 2018, the Man City bus was attacked with bottles, bricks and flares ahead of a Champions League meeting between the two sides, with future fixtures in Liverpool at times seeing the players' bus route amended to avoid throngs of home fans.

In March 2025, Merseyside police requested an unorthodox kick-off of 3.45pm for the match, rather than the customary Sunday start time of 4.30pm, in a bid to reduce challenges between the two sets of fans.

Top five football betting tips and tricks

📅 31 Aug 2018 | ⏱️ 4 min read (783 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well.
  • Sources indicate that getting started on football betting is far from easy, though.
  • Recent findings suggest that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Sources indicate that getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

Recent findings suggest that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having remarked that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it notable to follow the action closely?

Industry observers note that first of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

In a recent development, as you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

Industry observers note that favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

Sources indicate that if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier mentioned than done, though.

In a recent development, whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

Cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is right now playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

Sources indicate that his son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

Il centrocampista piace a Palladino, che lo ha già allenato alla Fiorentina; Bondo è l’alternativa per gennaio.

It has been revealed that danilo Cataldi è il primo nome nella lista del Bologna per rinforzare il centrocampo a gennaio. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, L’ipotesi dipende però da due condizioni: che il giocatore abbia superato del tutto il problema fisico con cui ha convissuto negli ultimi mesi e che le richieste di Claudio Lotito per il suo cartellino non siano troppo alte. Il contratto del centrocampista con la Lazio scade a giugno. Se la pista non dovesse concretizzarsi, l’alternativa indicata è Warren Bondo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

il Bologna considera Cataldi una soluzione gradita e fattibile. Il club punta ad acquistare un mediano alla riapertura del mercato di gennaio, una necessità nota già da agosto.

Sources indicate that L’interesse del Bologna per Cataldi non nasce ora. Gli uomini dell’area tecnica avevano già pensato di portarlo a Casteldebole nell’anno in cui il centrocampista della Lazio passò invece alla Fiorentina. In viola trovò come allenatore Raffaele Palladino e disputò una grande stagione.

Tra il tecnico e Cataldi c’è stima reciproca. Palladino sarebbe felice di allenarlo di nuovo e anche il centrocampista ha grande considerazione di lui. Giovanni Sartori e Marco Di Vaio, per il momento, non vogliono affrontare pubblicamente il tema del mercato. La fonte ritiene possibile che si siano già mossi per capire prima le intenzioni del giocatore e poi quelle della Lazio.

Per il Bologna, dunque, Cataldi resta la prima scelta, a condizione che il guaio fisico sia completamente alle spalle e che l’eventuale trattativa con Lotito sia sostenibile. Il centrocampista ha 32 anni e arriverà a scadenza contrattuale a giugno.

Se non dovessero esserci le condizioni per arrivare a Cataldi, il Bologna guarda a Warren Bondo. Il centrocampista è attualmente fuori rosa al Milan, dopo aver trascorso il campionato passato nella Cremonese. Anche lui ha già lavorato con Palladino, ai tempi del Monza.

Industry observers note that rispetto a Cataldi, Bondo è un classe 2003 e non occuperebbe un posto in lista. I due profili hanno inoltre un elemento in comune: conoscono il campionato italiano. Palladino e il Bologna cercano rinforzi che non debbano impiegare tempo per adattarsi alla realtà del calcio italiano.

Per quanto possibile, lo stesso criterio guiderà la ricerca di giocatori destinati agli altri reparti. Il discorso è più complicato soprattutto per gli attaccanti: in Italia, chi dispone di profili affidabili tende a trattenerli oppure chiede cifre che il Bologna non è disposto a spendere.

  • "Notre coach, Jean-Michel Picollet (photo), était à fond pour les Verts.

Dans Le Patriote du Beaujolais, l'ancien gardien et capitaine caladois Franck Laurent se remémore son 16e de finale de Coupe de France perdu en aux tirs au buts contre les Verts (2-2, 1-3 tab). Extraits.

"Notre coach, Jean-Michel Picollet (photo), était à fond pour les Verts. C'était le derby pour nous. On était tellement contents de tomber sur eux ! Je me souviens encore de la causerie du coach, comme si c'était hier. Son message était clair et net. On allait respecter Saint-Etienne à 200% mais par contre, on allait jouer notre match à fond. Le coach nous disait qu'il y avait un truc à faire. Il nous avait mis dans cette position-là, mentalement on était prêt. On en a profité un maximum. Sur un match, on avait nos chances. On jouait sur notre terrain. Eux n'avaient pas l'habitude de ce genre de pelouse. Il y a des facteurs, dans ce genre de match, qui font que tu transcendes, que tu te mets au niveau de l'événement, tu joues ta chance à fond.

Recent findings suggest that ce match, on en parlait tous les jours entre nous. Du début à la fin, on a vécu les choses à fond ! Ce match-là, contre Saint-Etienne, ça fait 16 ans qu'il a été joué. On m'en parle régulièrement. Pourtant, je ne suis plus du tout dans le foot. Quand on se croise, entre joueurs de cette époque, les premiers mots portent toujours sur ce match. On est liés à vie avec cette aventure de Coupe de France. C'est un petit bout de l'histoire du FCVB. J'ai eu la chance d'être là, au bon moment. Dans une carrière, ce n'est pas si évident de laisser des traces pareilles dans un club !

Sources indicate that les conseils que je donnerais aux Caladois d'aujourd'hui avant d'aller à Geoffroy Guichard, ce samedi ? Le contexte est totalement différent. C'est une Ligue 2 contre une Ligue 3. Il y a des joueurs professionnels des deux côtés. Je ne sais pas si je peux leur donner un conseil, à mon niveau. Mais même pour eux, ça reste des matches magnifiques à vivre. J'espère qu'ils vont arriver à s'extraire du championnat pour profiter pleinement de ce match, et tout donner. Derrière, ça peut renforcer le groupe.".

Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

📅 30 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.
  • Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five.
  • But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that “The data is not notable,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”.

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

Industry observers note that “After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”.

Recent findings suggest that it is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl.

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

Industry observers note that “I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Sources indicate that caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

Recent findings suggest that “We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso stated. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”.

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Recent findings suggest that macPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

In a recent development, fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they revealed it in certain moments of the game.”.

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert.

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D.

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

But in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Industry observers note that dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

#166036. Opinion: The morality of football

Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1287 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • According to recent reports, is football a moral force for good?
  • Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

According to recent reports, is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

Recent findings suggest that in not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

According to recent reports, in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

According to recent reports, if humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Industry observers note that furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

According to recent reports, the overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

In a recent development, football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

According to recent reports, the desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise vital questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 17:31 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 04:29 EST, 24 November 2026.

David Moyes’ record-breaking night as Everton manager could not have been more miserable.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record for most games in the dugout.

But that was about the only positive he could take away from the Gtech Community Stadium, as high-flying Brentford battered ten-man Everton on an evening to forget for the 63-year-old Scotsman.

Daily Mail Sport's Bobby Manzi was at the Gtech Community Stadium on a torrid night for the Toffees...

The Bees can mix it with substantial boys.

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again.

They climbed to sixth, leapfrogging Leeds — who have had far more praise lavished on them this season than Keith Andrews’ reliable side.

Brentford are disciplined with plenty of attacking flair, even with frontman and top goalscorer Igor Thiago suspended.

‘We set out this season looking to be better than last season, and if that happens, we will be flying to different destinations next season,’ Andrews said of their European hopes.’.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We've got a very competitive squad that strives to get better. If we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place.

‘I enjoyed us,’ he added about the performance. ‘I thought we were very good. We played with real bravery, courage and energy.’.

Sources indicate that brentford limited Everton to just three touches in the penalty area in the first half. They grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck and pinned their opponents back.

Jaidon Anthony was superb on the flank, providing two assists. Midfielder Vitaly Janelt capped off a brilliant display with a wonder strike from 25 yards, finding the top corner with his left foot.

Both of Keane Lewis-Potter’s goals had an element of fortune attached. But teams earn that luck when they manage ten shots in their opponents’ penalty area in just 45 minutes.

Lewis Potter starred at left-back, registering seven shots — the most of any player — and the joint-most touches in the opposition box. He was a menace and integral to every Brentford attack.

James Tarkowski endured a depressing return to his former club when he was shown the first Premier League red card of his career.

The speed and intensity of the tackle endangered his opponent. He had to go.

Referee Craig Pawson brandished a yellow, but a quick trip to the monitor saw it upgraded. Tarkowski ran down the tunnel before Pawson could even get the red card out of his pocket.

Everton were unbeaten in four games at Brentford before this and their defeat came in the form of the sublime and the ridiculous.

Maedine Makhloufi : "À la 89e dans le Chaudron ? Je vise le filet, tant pis pour Poteaux Carrés !"
