💡 Key Takeaways
  • Né à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez et formé à L’Étrat dès l'âge de 8 ans, Maedine Makhloufi avait signé son premier contrat professionnel avec les Verts en mai 2025 avant de mettre le cap sur Dunkerque l'hiver dernier.
  • According to recent reports, maedine, tu es né à deux pas de L'Étrat, à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez, et tu as poussé les portes de l’ASSE à seulement 8 ans.
  • Mon tout premier souvenir, c'est lors de ma détection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Né à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez et formé à L’Étrat dès l'âge de 8 ans, Maedine Makhloufi avait signé son premier contrat professionnel avec les Verts en mai 2025 avant de mettre le cap sur Dunkerque l'hiver dernier. Tout juste prêté au FC Villefranche Beaujolais (Ligue 3), le latéral gauche de 21 ans s'apprête à retrouver Geoffroy-Guichard dès ce samedi (19h) à l'occasion du 8e tour de la Coupe de France. Avant ces retrouvailles au goût forcément particulier, l'ancien protégé du centre de formation s'est confié en toute simplicité à Poteaux Carrés.

According to recent reports, maedine, tu es né à deux pas de L'Étrat, à Saint-Priest-en-Jarez, et tu as poussé les portes de l’ASSE à seulement 8 ans. Quel est ton premier souvenir de gamin en Vert ?

Mon tout premier souvenir, c'est lors de ma détection. J'arrivais de l'Olympique du Montcel, à La Ricamarie. On avait raté les détections pour la génération 2005, donc je les ai passées avec les 2006. À la fin, ils m'ont demandé si j'étais né en 2006, je leur ai répondu que j'étais de 2005 et ils m'ont dit de revenir le lendemain avec ma génération. Tout est parti de là. C’est un cousin qui m’avait emmené ce jour-là, il m'avait dit : « Tu vas venir t'entraîner ». À 8 ans, tu ne réalises pas vraiment où tu mets les pieds, j'étais juste venu jouer au foot et m'amuser.

Le foot, c'était déjà toute ta vie à cet âge-là ?

In a recent development, oui, depuis tout petit. J'avais toujours un ballon avec moi, dès que je pouvais. En bas de chez moi, il y avait un stade, donc on passait notre temps là-bas avec mon grand frère, mes nombreux cousins et les potes du quartier.

Durant tes douze années au centre, y a-t-il un éducateur qui t'a plus marqué que les autres ?

According to recent reports, franchement, je n'en ai pas un en particulier qui ressort. Je n'ai croisé que de bonnes personnes, on a vraiment été très bien entourés, ils ont tous été magnifiques. Quand je suis arrivé à l'école de foot, on s'entraînait encore au stade à Méons, juste à côté de Geoffroy-Guichard. Puis en U12, on a basculé au centre de formation à L’Étrat, c'est devenu plus carré, plus cadré. Il y a eu des saisons plus compliquées que d'autres, mais j'ai franchi toutes les étapes jusqu'à la réserve et mon premier contrat pro. Je n'en garde que du positif.

Quels sont tes souvenirs les plus forts de toutes ces années de formation ?

According to recent reports, les derbies contre l'Olympique Lyonnais, sans hésiter ! Chaque week-end de derby, même quand on était tout petits, c'était magnifique, toute la semaine était spéciale. Et puis tous les tournois, les moments de vie entre coéquipiers, ce ne sont que des super souvenirs.

According to recent reports, le 28 mai 2025, tu signes ton premier contrat professionnel avec ton club formateur. Qu'est-ce qui se passe dans la tête d'un enfant du Forez à ce moment-là ?

According to recent reports, C'est la récompense de tout le travail accompli. Avant tout, une immense fierté, pour moi mais surtout pour mes proches. On n'a pas fait de grosse fête particulière, mais tout le monde était heureux et j'ai senti que j'avais rendu ma famille fière.

Tu n'as pas paraphé ce contrat tout seul puisque Jules Mouton a signé le sien le même jour que toi. Vous vous êtes un peu chambrés ?

In a recent development, non, parce qu'on le savait un petit peu avant. Jules est arrivé un an après moi, on a fait pratiquement tout notre parcours ensemble, donc arriver là main dans la main, c'était magnifique. On est restés très proches. Je garde d'ailleurs le contact avec la plupart des gars de la génération 2005 sur les réseaux. Avec Jules, on s'est même croisés en Ligue 2 cette saison puisqu'il joue à Grenoble, on a un peu rigolé avant le match.

Qu'est-ce qui a motivé ton départ vers Dunkerque au mercato d'hiver dernier ?

Recent findings suggest that J'ai reçu un appel de Dunkerque et ça s'est fait très vite. À Saint-Étienne, je n'avais pas beaucoup de temps de jeu : je jouais en réserve mais pas du tout avec l'équipe première. C'était une belle opportunité pour moi, les deux clubs se sont mis d'accord sans aucun problème.

Après douze ans dans le cocon stéphanois, comment s'est passée ton intégration dans le Nord ?

According to recent reports, super bien, franchement nickel. À Saint-Étienne, je m'étais déjà pas mal entraîné avec le groupe pro, donc rien qu'en observant les anciens, tu apprends vite. Et à Dunkerque, le groupe était jeune avec que des bons mecs. Bon, comme on est tout près de la mer, il y a souvent du vent, mais on s'y fait (rires) !

Sources indicate that là-bas, tu as choisi de porter le numéro 42. C'était un message subliminal pour dire que la Loire ne te quittait jamais ?

(Rires) Oui, c'était clairement un clin d'œil ! Comme je suis arrivé en cours de saison, il ne restait plus énormément de numéros libres et j'ai tout de suite sauté sur le 42. J'ai reçu plein de messages sympas de supporters stéphanois grâce à ça, et même dans le Nord, tout le monde savait à quoi ça correspondait !

In a recent development, même si tu aurais aimé jouer davantage, tu as quand même eu le temps de marquer un but express en 4 minutes dans un derby face à Boulogne ! Qu'as-tu appris chez les Maritimes ?

Industry observers note that C'était une sensation incroyable, mon premier but chez les pros et dans un derby en plus, tu ne peux pas rêver mieux ! Ces mois à Dunkerque m'ont fait basculer du monde semi-pro au monde pro. J'ai énormément appris sur les détails tactiques, l'exigence de concentration et l'impact physique. La réserve en N3 te prépare bien parce que tu affrontes des adultes, mais l'étage au-dessus, c'est encore un autre monde.

Tu viens tout juste de poser tes valises au FC Villefranche Beaujolais en prêt pour retrouver du rythme en Ligue 3. Passer de la mer du Nord aux vignes du Beaujolais, le choc climatique et gastronomique n'est pas trop rude ?

(Rires) Non, franchement ça va très bien ! En plus, je me rapproche de la maison. Et puis dans le Beaujolais, on mange bien et on boit bien aussi, donc l'adaptation est facile.

Tu es arrivé lundi dernier à Villefranche, et le tirage au sort t'envoie directement dans le Chaudron ce samedi ! Tu as vérifié que la FFF n'avait pas truqué les boules juste pour ton histoire personnelle ?

It has been revealed that C'est possible ça (rires) ! Non, plus sérieusement, c'est un scénario magnifique. J'ai déjà eu la chance de rejouer 5 ou 10 minutes à Geoffroy-Guichard avec Dunkerque la saison dernière, et revenir chez moi devant ma famille et mes amis, c'était quelque chose de fort. Ce samedi, mes proches seront encore en tribunes. Maintenant, je ne suis pas le coach, j'espère avant tout être dans le groupe et avoir du temps de jeu.

Pour les supporters stéphanois qui t'ont un peu perdu de vue, quel joueur es-tu devenu aujourd'hui dans ton couloir gauche ?

J'ai beaucoup travaillé sur mes défauts depuis mon départ à Dunkerque, on avait ciblé certains points précis et je me suis accroché. J'ai gagné en expérience et en maturité, dans mon jeu comme en dehors. Aujourd'hui, je suis un joueur plus complet et plus fort.

Qu'est-ce qui te motive au quotidien quand tu te lèves pour aller à l'entraînement ?

According to recent reports, je me dis simplement que j'ai l'un des plus beaux métiers du monde ! Il y a plein de gens qui se lèvent tôt pour faire des boulots bien plus difficiles que le nôtre, donc on n'a vraiment pas le droit de se plaindre. Même s'il y a toujours des séances plus dures que d'autres, je vais à l'entraînement avec le sourire. Le jour où je ne prendrai plus de plaisir, j'arrêterai.

Parmi les jeunes du centre qui sont aujourd'hui dans le groupe pro stéphanois, lequel redoutes-tu le plus d'affronter samedi soir ?

It has been revealed that ils ont tous beaucoup de qualités, mais je pense forcément à Kevin Pedro. On a un an d'écart, on a énormément joué ensemble et on était très proches. Il fait une saison magnifique et ça ne m'étonne pas du tout : il a toujours été très fort et joue avec beaucoup d'intelligence. Tout ce qui lui arrive est amplement mérité.

Recent findings suggest that dernière question : imaginons qu'on joue la 89e minute samedi, qu'il y a toujours 0-0 et que tu te retrouves seul face au gardien vert. Tu vises la lucarne pour qualifier Villefranche ou tu rends hommage à notre site en frappant volontairement sur le poteau carré — même s'ils sont ronds aujourd'hui ?

In a recent development, (Éclat de rire) Je pense que je vais plutôt viser le filet ! Tant pis pour Poteaux Carrés.

In a recent development, un grand merci à toi Maedine pour ta disponibilité. Toute l'équipe de Poteaux Carrés te souhaite le meilleur pour la suite et de pouvoir fouler la pelouse samedi… sans marquer si possible !

According to recent reports, merci beaucoup à vous ! Quel que soit le résultat, ce sera une belle fête. Sur un match de Coupe, l'écart entre une Ligue 2 et une Ligue 3 n'est pas si grand, tout reste possible.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Ajax moved into a clear second place in the Eredivisie with a routine 3-0 win against ADO Den Haag, as Feyenood slipped to fifth after losing to local rivals Excelsior.

Davy Klaassen took just three minutes to stroke home the opening goal for Ajax and added a second just before half-time.

By then ADO had been reduced to 10 men following the dismissal of Matteo Waem for hauling down Tolu Arakodare.

But there was a blow for Ajax ahead of next weekend’s visit to Feyenoord when Jorthy Mokio, scorer of the second goal, was taken off injured after an accidental collision with Sékou Sylla.

Feyenoord, who started the month top of the Eredivisie, suffered their first home defeat in the derby against Excelsior since 1980 to continue a slump in form that has seen them draw two and lose four of their last six games.

According to recent reports, givairo Read’s blistering shot gave Feyenoord the lead after just two minutes, but Excelsior were ahead by half-time and made it 3-1 when Casper Windell headed in a corner after 58 minutes. Despite an own goal by Jan Plug, on loan from Feyenoord, Excelsior were not to be denied.

PSV remain a point clear of Ajax at the top of the table after they cruised to a 4-1 win at NEC, with Filip Kostic opening the scoring with his first goal for PSV and his first Eredivisie goal since 2014, when he was playing for Groningen.

Utrecht sacked their managed Anthony Correia after just 14 matches after sinking to 15th place in the table with a 3-2 home defeat to Cambuur.

Correia won just four games after leaving Telstar, the club he led to promotion two seasons ago and where he spent his entire 15-year playing career. Youth team coach Mark Otten will take charge of the first team while Utrecht search for a replacement.

Willem II, searching for their first Eredivisie win in 30 matches, took a shock lead away to Twente despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half when Devin Haen was given space in the area to shoot past Joël Drommel.

The home side struggled to turn their superiority into goals, but an equaliser by Ramiz Zerrouki and a late header by Marko Pjaca gave them the points they needed to rise to third place above Feyenoord.

AZ also overtook Feyenoord as they beat Sparta 5-1 with a dominant second-half display, while Fortuna Sittard kept in touch with the leading group with a typically gritty 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles.

Go Ahead Eagles 0-1 Fortuna Sittard.

Sparta Rotterdam 1-5 AZ Alkmaar.

Twente Enschede 2-1 Willem II Tilburg.

It has been revealed that comme on l'escomptait, Sainté a profité de la faiblesse de l'adversité pour lancer sa belle saison en cours. Sans surprise, les trois premiers adversaires de la saison des Verts occupent actuellement les trois dernières places du classement. Avant-dernier avec le même nombre de points (11) que le barragiste clermontois et de la lanterne rouge grenobloise, le FC Sochaux est dans une très mauvaise dynamique, qui a conduit son président Clément Calvez à s'exprimer dans la dernière édition de L'Est Républicain. Extraits.

"Cela ne fait jamais plaisir de perdre un match, alors cinq d'affilée... On se pose beaucoup de questions. On est au-delà du stade de la préoccupation et on se creuse les méninges pour trouver des solutions. Ce qui a fait notre force, notre solidarité, notre engagement, on l'a un peu perdu. Je ne pense pas que ce soit un relâchement dans le travail, peut-être un peu dans les têtes. Il faut remettre le bleu de chauffe. Ce n'est surtout pas le moment de partir en vrille, de commencer à chercher des coupables, de regarder le voisin de travers. On doit tous être unis, faire notre autocritique et avancer comme un seul homme. Si la question du maintien de Vincent Hognon se pose ? On considère que changer d'entraîneur n'est pas la solution. Au contraire, il faut faire le dos rond pour sortir de cette mauvaise passe.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Marathon skater Judith Krabbenborg has taken advantage of the early cold snap to smash the world one-hour record for skating on natural ice.

The 29-year-old took to the ice in Winterswijk, Gelderland, at 8.30am on Tuesday and covered a distance of 34 kilometres 878 metres, beating the previous women’s record by 2.6 kilometres.

“I could feel my legs and my back hurting at the end, but there were so many people standing on the sidelines that it gave me energy,” she told NOS.

According to recent reports, the previous record, set four years ago by Femke Mossinkoff, also in Winterswijk, was the first official time for the hour by a woman on natural ice. On the same day Bart Vreugdenhil set the current men’s record of 36 kilometers 717 metres.

Most skating records are set on artificial ice, but Winterswijk is one of three arenas where the local club has been able to create a natural arena for early-morning skaters during the recent cold weather.

The all-time women’s record is 40 kilometres 569 metres, set by another Dutch skater, Carien Kleibeuker, in Inzell, Austria, in 2015.

The rink at Winterswijk closed a few hours after Krabbenborg’s record-breaking skate as the ice started to melt, but it is expected to be available again on Wednesday morning.

Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

📅 30 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

In a recent development, their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

In a recent development, ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT.

Sources indicate that defensive rebuilding is next summer’s major project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k.

According to recent reports, united were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD.

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR.

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick stated. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”.

Industry observers note that there was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

According to recent reports, asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”.

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”.

Industry observers note that and on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He demonstrated his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

According to recent reports, “We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”.

Speaking with Sky Sports, he noted: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

According to recent reports, “To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

In a recent development, “It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

In a recent development, “But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

It has been revealed that “We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”.

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx.

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ.

According to recent reports, the hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

In a recent development, “Scoring before half-time is always vital if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”.

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283.

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk.

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV.

In a recent development, dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

It has been revealed that man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

According to recent reports, the Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

In a recent development, five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Industry observers note that fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

It has been revealed that mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR.

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

Recent findings suggest that the Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb.

Sources indicate that what a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Sources indicate that harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k.

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you….

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa.

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

Sources indicate that we are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Recent findings suggest that ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

Recent findings suggest that end-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ.

Recent findings suggest that there will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD.

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

According to recent reports, you would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Sources indicate that ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

It has been revealed that and United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

According to recent reports, what a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

In a recent development, ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT.

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

It has been revealed that davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

In a recent development, there’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second substantial save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Recent findings suggest that rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Recent findings suggest that chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Industry observers note that maeda indicates a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Ipswich get us under way through Enciso.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Recent findings suggest that carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The upcoming £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

According to recent reports, carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz.

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

"He's a fantastic footballer." Ashley Young discusses Marcus Rashford 🔊 pic.twitter.com/4hYAtx9zZF.

Michael Carrick explains the changes to his Man Utd starting XI to face Ipswich 🔴Watch the game live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/p9FD36h3OM.

It has been revealed that against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

Recent findings suggest that when Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

Recent findings suggest that the hosts will also need captain Bruno Fernandes to deliver. He will levels below his exceptionally high standards last time out, while Bryan Mbeumo also needs to make more of an impact.

It was short and not sweet. Playing in their first top-flight campaign since 2001-02, Ipswich finished 19th with just 22 points under Kieran McKenna.

This time, Gary O’Neil is the boss and they’ve already ticked off one victory thanks to those three points against Sunderland.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

According to recent reports, martinez and Dalot are two alterations in Man Utd’s backline, replacing Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui. Gary Neville feels the club’s defence could let them down this season.

"You can get at them" ❌Gary Neville has concerns over Manchester United's defence for the upcoming season particularly after defeat to Hull 🤔 pic.twitter.com/v3sEjInI2j.

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

It has been revealed that against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

"I wouldn't say massive concerns, but he will be worried""If Carrick doesn't see a reaction today, there is a problem"The Manchester United players will be under pressure to perform, states Ashley Young 📈 pic.twitter.com/dR6uat4l2P.

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

Gary O’Neil has named an unchanged line-up from the side that beat Sunderland last week. Recent signing Exequiel Palacios is on the bench after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.

In a recent development, your Town at Old Trafford! ✊ pic.twitter.com/mVMj2LVNvs.

Unsurprisingly, Michael Carrick has shuffled his pack after last weekend’s disastrous defeat to Hull. Rashford, Mainoo, Martinez and Dalot all come into the starting X1.

U-N-I-T-E-D.The team for us ❤️📋.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

According to recent reports, man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

Recent findings suggest that when the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”.

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

La Lazio non ha espresso una preferenza; alle precedenti elezioni fu l’unico club di Serie A ad astenersi.

Almeno 11 club di Serie A sostengono Giovanni Malagò nella corsa alla presidenza della FIGC, mentre Adriano Galliani raccoglie il sostegno di un altro fronte. Secondo quanto riportato da Calcio e Finanza, La Lega Serie A, che alle precedenti elezioni aveva promosso la candidatura dell’ex numero uno del CONI con uno schieramento compatto, rischia di uscire dalla nuova tornata elettorale divisa al proprio interno.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Il numero dei club favorevoli a Malagò è rilevante per la sua candidatura: per presentarla serve infatti l’appoggio di almeno una componente. Il fronte pro Galliani, guidato dal presidente interista, potrebbe dunque trovarsi in minoranza.

La scelta del prossimo presidente federale resta aperta tra i due candidati. La divisione nella massima serie riguarda anche gli equilibri interni della Lega in vista delle elezioni dei consiglieri federali.

According to recent reports, secondo quanto riportato dal Corriere dello Sport, alcuni club si sono allontanati dallo schieramento favorevole a Malagò, Atalanta e Inter in testa. Tra le società ancora indecise figurano anche Juventus e Milan.

In a recent development, alle differenze sulla presidenza della FIGC potrebbe quindi aggiungersi un’ulteriore frattura al momento di eleggere i consiglieri federali. È su entrambi i passaggi che si misura la compattezza mostrata dalla Serie A nella precedente tornata.

'Bitter' Romelu Lukaku set to 'drop a bombshell' on Belgian football following his shock retirement, claims former team-mate after one-hour phone call

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (969 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.
  • Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly revealed his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.

Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly revealed his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.

Belgium's all-time record goalscorer had been left on the bench against Italy, while he had not been in the squad three days earlier for the match against Turkey.

Lukaku's shock announcement caught Belgian media by surprise, while his former international team-mate Nainggolan has claimed more news will follow from the star.

Nainggolan, who won 30 caps for the national team between 2009 and 2018, revealed on the Ongefilterd Voetbal podcast he had a one-hour phone call with Lukaku following his decision.

The former Inter Milan and Roma midfielder stated that Lukaku told him: 'You are only allowed to say that a bombshell is about to explode.'.

Romelu Lukaku announced his shock retirement from international football earlier this month.

Former team-mate Radja Nainggolan claims Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement for Belgian football following a one hour phone call with the star. Source: Ongefilterd Voetbal.

'So something is still coming,' Nainggolan said.

Industry observers note that 'What? I don't know. There were some internal problems between him and a certain person. But I'm not going to say much about that.

Industry observers note that 'Romelu will bring that up himself. He was a bit bitter, though. He was disappointed, frustrated.

'We will hear from him soon what will happen.

'About the real problems that were at play, he will be able to explain that better than I.'.

Lukaku's retirement had marked a stunning reversal of his prepares, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United forward having vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku had confirmed his international retirement on social media.

It has been revealed that '16 years old', his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

According to recent reports, 'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

Industry observers note that 'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking onto the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retired as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the 2026 World Cup under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute – and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

Sources indicate that 'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he remarked.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

La Calade des gens heureux

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Poteaux-carres

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, heureux comme tous les membres du FC Villefranche Beaujolais d'affronter les Verts dans le Chaudron après-demain soir, le président caladois Philippe Terrier s'est confié ce jeudi à BFM.
  • "A 48 heures de la rencontre, on sent que ça commence à monter.
  • Industry observers note that J'ai accepté d'être président en 2010, le jour où on a joué contre Saint-Étienne.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, heureux comme tous les membres du FC Villefranche Beaujolais d'affronter les Verts dans le Chaudron après-demain soir, le président caladois Philippe Terrier s'est confié ce jeudi à BFM. Extraits.

"A 48 heures de la rencontre, on sent que ça commence à monter. Au club, les gens en parlent de plus en plus. Il y a l'effervescence qui est en train de venir et il y a beaucoup de monde qui va se déplacer. C'est un véritable moment de bonheur qu'on est en train de vivre. C'est le sujet de conversation à Villefranche, en Calade, cette semaine. Il y a eu le marathon qui était un véritable succès. Derrière, on enclenche avec ce match qui restera historique. Il y aura entre 2 000 et 3 000 Caladois qui vont faire le déplacement. On attend 20 000 personnes dans le stade. Il va falloir faire du bruit pour se faire entendre.

Industry observers note that J'ai accepté d'être président en 2010, le jour où on a joué contre Saint-Étienne. On avait fait match nul à la fin du temps réglementaire. Puis, après les prolongations, on avait perdu aux tirs au but. Mais le moment était tellement merveilleux que quand l'ancien président s'est tourné vers moi et m'a demandé si j'acceptais le poste... Avec l'euphorie, j’ai dit oui. C'est le lendemain que j'ai compris que j'avais fait une bêtise, mais sur le moment, je pensais avoir bien fait. Une bêtise qui dure quand même, parce que ça fait 16 ans que je suis resté.

Aujourd'hui, c'est un bonheur. 16 ans après, on retrouve Saint-Étienne sur notre parcours.C'est beau quand même. C'est assez émouvant. Mais cette fois, ce sera à Geoffroy-Guichard, dans le Chaudron. L’ASSE, c'est une véritable équipe de Ligue 1. C'est une équipe qui pourrait rivaliser avec beaucoup d'équipes du niveau supérieur. Sur un match de Coupe de France, on sait que tout est possible. On part à 50-50 et on verra bien.

Recent findings suggest that on a encaissé 4 buts lors d enotre match contre Bastia. Il faudra que notre défense soit beaucoup plus solide et surtout beaucoup plus concentrée. Parce qu'il y a eu beaucoup d'erreurs sur les quatre buts qu'on a pris. Il y a eu beaucoup d'erreurs d'attention. Je pense que les joueurs seront beaucoup plus concentrés à Saint-Etienne. Mais les adversaires seront d'une autre taille, c'est ça le problème !

Le message que j’ai passé tout au long de la semaine aux joueurs, c’est avant tout, de se faire plaisir et de se dire que c'est possible. Que sur un match, ils peuvent être au niveau.Un exploit, c'est tellement beau à vivre qu'il faut qu’ils vivent ce moment avec intensité. On verra bien ce qui se passera. Les joueurs vont jouer à 110 ou 120 % de leurs moyens. Parfois, il y a une équipe en face qui ne peut jouer qu'à 90 % de ses moyens. La motivation n'est pas la même. C'est aussi une façon pour les joueurs de montrer qu'on ne s'est pas trompés quand on les a recrutés et qu'ils sont bien meilleurs que ce qu'ils ont proposé jusqu'à présent. On sait qu'ils seront présents.

Recent findings suggest that L'état d'esprit du groupe, c’est vraiment le travail, le travail, le travail ! Il faut qu'on corrige tout ce qu'on a mal fait. Il faut qu'on soit bon samedi. Le coach se charge de leur mettre un peu la pression. Je sais que tout le Rhône va être derrière le FCVB samedi, ça va au-delà de la Calade. On a eu la chance de jouer au Groupama Stadium en 2019 contre le PSG. C'était quelque chose d'incroyable. L'autre stade dans lequel j'espérais faire un match un jour, c'était Geoffroy Guichard. Donc, avant tout, c'est une fête.

In a recent development, la Coupe de France, c'est un objectif. Je l'ai dit aux joueurs, je l'ai dit au groupe. Il faut aller le plus loin possible parce qu'il y a encore le souvenir de l'an dernier, de cette sortie de route très tôt face à un club de R3. On a 650 partenaires, le meilleur moyen de les récompenser, c'est de faire quelque chose de phénoménal en Coupe de France. On pioche en championnat. Si on offre à nos partenaires une victoire contre Saint-Etienne, ce serait juste l'euphorie dans la ville.

Le Caladois est un peu chauvin. Si on le fait, ce serait le top. On peut le faire ! C'est déjà un très beau cadeau de jouer contre Saint-Etienne. Si on va plus loin, c'est l’apothéose ! Je n'ai pas vraiment préparé ce que je vais dire aux joueurs samedi avant la rencontre, mais je vais avant tout leur demander de tout donner, et que quel que soit le résultat, qu'on soit fier d'eux et qu'on puisse dire qu'ils ont donné tout ce qu'ils avaient dans le ventre pour présenter un beau spectacle.".

Bosz indicates PSV were “trampled” after Real hit five in second half

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

PSV and Feyenoord face an uphill task to reach the group stages of the Champions League after defeats on Tuesday night saw them drop out of the qualifying places.

In a recent development, PSV briefly threatened to cause an upset in Madrid as they took a 1-0 lead into the half-time break. Ivan Perisic’s penalty after 32 minutes was their only reward for a courageous first-half display in which Ruben van Bommel and Sven Mijnans also missed clear chances to score.

But the introduction of Jude Bellingham at half-time changed the picture as Real’s superstars regrouped to score five goals. The England midfielder’s dazzling volley was the pick of the bunch, while Kylian Mbappé bagged a double and Vinicius Junior also got on the scoresheet.

Head coach Peter Bosz admitted his team had been “trampled underfoot” in the second half. “I think you had to be there to see how big the difference was between the first and second half,” he said.

“In the first half we were brave, put our opponents under pressure and had three massive chances in the first four minutes.

Recent findings suggest that “When you look at the second half, they scored rapidly and the tempo of their game was much higher. That’s the quality they have with the players they can bring off the bench.”.

PSV’s next match is a home tie against Real’s city rivals Atletico on December 9, before they travel to Stavanger to take on Viking in January and round off the group stage at home to Stuttgart.

Feyenoord suffered a narrower defeat at home to Porto as they were unable to recover from an own goal after two minutes by Oussama Targhalline.

Goalkeeper Florian Kastenmeier vindicated the decision of Giovanni van Bronckhorst to replace the out-of-form Tjark Ernst by making some vital saves to keep the Rotterdammers in the game.

Feyenoord staged a late rally, with Gjivai Zechiël going close and Targhalline striking the crossbar from long range, but they were unable to breach the Portuguese side’s defence.

The fans in De Kuip were briefly celebrating after a bizarre incident when referee Irfan Peltjo’s watch told him a header by Nacho Ferri had crossed the line, but video replays clearly demonstrated it bounced off the post and into the hands of Diogo Costa.

It has been revealed that feyenoord have just three points from their five matches so far, one less than PSV. Their next two matches are away to Viking on December 8 and Galatasaray on January 19, before they close their campaign in Rotterdam against RB Leipzig.

La Serie A eleggerà tre consiglieri federali il 14 dicembre, ma i candidati sono cinque. Ai tre uscenti Stefano Campoccia, Giorgio Chiellini e Giuseppe Marotta si sono aggiunti Saverio Sticchi Damiani e il presidente della Lazio Claudio Lotito. Tra le ipotesi in vista del voto c’è anche quella di preferenze disgiunte tra la presidenza FIGC e il Consiglio federale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that nel breve mandato di Malagò, i posti spettanti alla massima serie erano occupati da Campoccia, dell’Udinese, Chiellini, della Juventus, e Marotta, dell’Inter. Tutti e tre si sono ricandidati. Con loro correranno il presidente del Lecce Sticchi Damiani e Lotito, che punta a tornare nell’incarico già ricoperto.

It has been revealed that come riferisce il Corriere dello Sport, il quadro delle candidature si inserisce in una Serie A attraversata da divisioni. Alcuni club sono usciti dal fronte Malagò, con Atalanta e Inter in testa. Tra gli indecisi figurano anche Juventus e Milan; in vista delle elezioni dei consiglieri federali, le fratture interne potrebbero allargarsi.

Industry observers note that ogni società di Serie A può indicare un candidato al Consiglio federale. Nelle precedenti elezioni Chiellini aveva ottenuto sette voti e Marotta sei, in una situazione descritta come praticamente opposta a quella attuale.

Il fronte favorevole a Galliani, guidato dal presidente interista Marotta, potrebbe risentire della propria posizione di minoranza. I club che sostengono Malagò sono almeno 11: un sostegno necessario alla sua candidatura, per la quale serve l’appoggio di almeno una componente.

According to recent reports, in questo scenario, alcune società potrebbero scegliere il voto disgiunto: sostenere un candidato alla presidenza FIGC e, per il Consiglio federale, esprimere una preferenza per un nome non apertamente schierato con lui. L’esempio indicato è un voto per Malagò alla presidenza e per Marotta, primo sostenitore di Galliani, come consigliere. Una soluzione che richiederebbe un lavoro diplomatico.

Messi was a deity among Argentina’s unholy rabble

📅 31 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world.
  • Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could.
  • Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless New Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

And yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Industry observers note that today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Industry observers note that messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

In a recent development, “Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

In a recent development, you struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

Recent findings suggest that as a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose.

It has been revealed that to study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

Recent findings suggest that that alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

La possibilità di guidare gli azzurri lo attirava molto. Il tecnico ha spiegato quanto avrebbe significato per lui accettare l'incarico: «Sarebbe stato uno dei più grandi onori della mia carriera allenare la nazionale italiana».

Alla base del rifiuto c'era la stanchezza. Guardiola arrivava da dieci anni al Manchester City, durante i quali aveva conquistato sei campionati e una Champions League. Alle spalle aveva inoltre 18 anni complessivi in panchina, scanditi da partite ogni tre giorni.

Sentiva così il bisogno di prendersi una pausa. Nel raccontare quella decisione, ha detto: «Mi sono reso conto che dovevo smettere. Avevo bisogno di un po' di tempo per me stesso».

It has been revealed that "Cette semaine j'ai axé nos séances sur le dépassement de soi. Après, est-ce que ça se verra en match ? C'est toujours pareil. Ce match, tu peux le jouer 50 fois, tu le perdras 49 fois ! La seule chose à prendre en compte, c'est de savoir si nous serons dans la seule fois où nous pouvons gagner ce match.

Si tu ne joues pas pleinement ce match, tu n'en joueras aucun. Dans la logique, tu n'as rien à perdre parce que tout est perdu depuis le début ! Tu as vraiment tout à gagner. Le tour d'avant, quand Saint-Etienne a joué contre Rumilly, il leur manquait 12 internationaux. Là, ce sera tout autre-chose. C'est une machine de guerre ! C'est équilibré, ça court vite, ça possède de la mobilité, ça saute haut, ça presse, ça met de l'intensité. C'est une équipe de Ligue 1. Dans ma tête, j'y vais pour gagner, c'est normal. Mais dans l'absolu si tu perds, ce ne sera pas un exploit pour eux.".

According to recent reports, la FIGC rinnova il suo impegno contro la violenza sulle donne con una campagna di sensibilizzazione affidata a sei calciatori e calciatrici e ribadisce l’invito alle vittime di violenza o stalking a chiamare il 1522. Secondo quanto riportato da Figc, L’iniziativa è legata alla Giornata internazionale per l’eliminazione della violenza sulle donne. Lo riferisce la FIGC.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, gianluigi Donnarumma, Cristiana Girelli, Laura Giuliani, Pio Esposito, Riccardo Calafiori e Annamaria Serturini sono i protagonisti della comunicazione della Federazione. La campagna affronta la violenza di genere in tutte le sue forme: non soltanto gli episodi di cronaca, ancora troppo frequenti, ma anche la dimensione culturale e sociale del fenomeno, legata agli stereotipi e al mancato riconoscimento della libertà e dell’autonomia delle donne.

In a recent development, il messaggio distingue la violenza da ciò che può essere presentato come una lite, il controllo dalla gelosia e il possesso dalla protezione: «È una lite? No, è violenza. È gelosia? No, è controllo. È protezione? No, è possesso». A queste domande la campagna affianca una risposta: il numero 1522.

Il 1522 è un servizio gratuito di pubblica utilità istituito nel 2006 dal Dipartimento per le Pari Opportunità. Il suo obiettivo è favorire l’emersione e il contrasto della violenza contro le donne, sia all’interno sia all’esterno della famiglia, attraverso un’ampia azione di sistema.

In occasione della Giornata internazionale, la FIGC torna quindi a invitare le vittime di ogni forma di violenza o stalking a comporre il numero.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a new raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.
  • Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026.

Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a new raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.

If the move is approved, it is likely to trigger a flood of cash in the market similar to the massive £765million spree in 2023 that saw the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and N'Golo Kante sign for Public Investment Fund (PIF) teams.

In that 2023 window, almost half of the transfer fees received by Premier League clubs came from the SPL.

In total, 94 players were signed by Pro League clubs and the January transfer window could now follow a similar pattern.

The Saudi spending reached such astronomic levels that it eclipsed every other league in Europe aside from the Premier League.

Cristiano Ronaldo (right) and Angelo, pictured in action for Al Nassr, are among the foreign stars already plying their trade in Saudi Arabia and more will be on their way.

The supposed reason for the proposed rule change is to elevate the standard of existing Saudi players at home by raising the overall level of talent ahead of the country hosting the World Cup in 2034.

But critics argue that the newly introduced rules would only force Saudi players out of their domestic league in place of high-profile foreign recruits.

While Premier League clubs are often reluctant to allow talent to leave in January midway through the season, the fees on offer from Saudi can be eye-watering and hard to turn down.

Aston Villa sold Jhon Duran and later Ollie Watkins for a combined £115million to the SPL.

Fulham accepted £50m for Aleksandar Mitrovic, while Wolves banked £47m for Ruben Neves and Liverpool were able to recoup almost £50m for Darwin Nunez.

West Ham were able to cash in on Crysencio Summerville after relegation last term when Al Hilal bought him for £60m.

Recent findings suggest that would Man United consider offers for Bruno Fernandes as his contract winds down? Or will they keep the club captain to help battle relegation?

Suddenly every Premier League club recruitment department will be reassessing their squads and be keeping a close eye on the rule developments in Saudi.

Ollie Watkins moved from Aston Villa to Al Hilal and the Premier League side have recouped huge fees from the SPL in the  past.

Ivan Toney (second from left) and his Al Ahli team-mates celebrate a goal against Al Nassr.

The SPL's decision on whether to allow the increase of foreign players will be clarified before the winter window opens.

The PIF are winding down their investment in golf through LIV having invested more than £3.7billion since 2021 but their operation in football demonstrates no sign of slowing down.

Players weighing up a move to Saudi will perhaps have a more difficult decision than in 2023 over relocating, with conflict still affecting the country.

The Asian Cup was postponed earlier in November following a missile attack from Yemen-based Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Security fears and geo-political uncertainty could make footballers think twice before accepting the lucrative contracts on offer in January and beyond.
